measurer_summary.question: A4: Error-signal survival. For each corpus and swechat format: how well does the native failure flag (native_error / exit_code) survive, what failure text survives and where, how well do ir.error_marker alone (A) and marker OR census regexes (B) agree with the native flag, does aiv_cu have any failure flag, and what error definition should Probe 3 use?

per_corpus.answer: is_error fill 4464/13592 = 0.328 [0.285,0.370] s126. It is filled on all 4150 shell results; non-shell results are only true (314) or absent (9128), so null means 'not flagged'. exit_code is never filled. Against native (null counted as negative): A has P 488/488, R 488/614 = 0.795 [0.72,0.85] s90. On shell, A has R 297/300 = 0.990 [0.97,1.00]; on non-shell, R 191/314 = 0.608 [0.52,0.69]. The non-shell misses are harness texts without a <tool_use_error> wrapper, e.g. 'File content exceeds' 27, 'File does not exist' 31, EISDIR 18. B adds 0 recall and 112 FP: P 488/600 = 0.813 [0.74,0.89]. Failure text is always in the result text: stderr-only hits = 0, and the exit header sits at the start 248/248. Proposed Probe 3 definition: native_error is True (null = not error).
per_corpus.decisive_number: A: precision 488/488, recall 0.795 [0.72,0.85] (n=614 native-true, 90 sessions); B adds 0 TP and 112 FP

per_corpus.answer: Native fill 3359/5164 = 0.650 [0.394,0.790] s107: shell 3312/3312, non-shell 47/1852. Native true 349. Of the 311 native-true shell results, 157 are cc_permission_denied (harness refusals) and 135 are cc_exit_code. Aggregates only. Proposed Probe 3 definition: native_error is True, split by marker class.

Its 1746 JSON turn records (output/error/system, the same harness as aiv_cu) are all native-null, with error non-empty on 267/1746 = 0.153 [0.098,0.236]. A: P 296/296, R 296/538 = 0.550 [0.34,0.79]. B: P 534/637 = 0.838 [0.74,0.90], R 534/538 = 0.993 [0.98,1.00] s38. B's gain is MCP 'Error:' text at the start (error_line text_start 201, 200 native true). Proposed Probe 3 definition: native_error is True, plus a separate unvalidated regex class on the village-bash JSON error field.

per_corpus.answer: Native fill 3735/3735 (status=error OR exit != 0). Shell exit_code 1135/1140, 157 nonzero. No marker exists (A R 0/197). The exit code does not survive into the IR text: B on shell has P 26/36 = 0.722, R 26/157 = 0.166 [0.10,0.25], and 24 native-true shell results have blank text. Non-shell 'Error:' lines at the start give B P 36/49 = 0.735 [0.47,0.87], R 36/40 = 0.900 [0.65,1.00]. Proposed Probe 3 definition: native_error only; the text proxy is dead for shell.

Native fill 2313/2313 from status: success 2170, error 126, cancelled 17. The text exit code and the native flag are DISJOINT. gemini_exit_code_nonzero fires on 280/816 shell results, all native false. Native-true results ('Failed to edit' 102, '[Operation Cancelled]' 17) match no family. A: P 0/280, R 0/143; B and C: P 0/281, R 0/143. Proposed Probe 3 definition: two classes, tool-call failure = native True and command failure = text exit code. The union cannot be validated. 10 sessions.

Native fill 265/265, 8 true (error_code=failure on all 8), 2 sessions. No marker. B: 1 TP, 1 FP, 7 FN, below the pre-registered minimum n. Proposed Probe 3 definition: native_error is True; text agreement is not measurable.
The source has no tool results: 0 results across 7 (cursor) and 4 (simple_text) A sessions. No error signal exists, so Probe 3 is dead for these formats.

No native failure field (0/6107). stderr is non-empty on 277/6107 = 0.045 [0.035,0.056]; shell 253/2229 = 0.114 [0.089,0.141]. On outputs that look successful, stderr is non-empty on 135/2698 = 0.050 [0.037,0.066] (shell 128/1888 = 0.068 [0.047,0.090]). Only 33/1888 = 0.017 [0.010,0.026] carry a failure template; the rest is mostly git/curl progress ('To https:' 41, 'From https:' 28). The 'system' key is present on 0/6107 results. output_null is structural for gui (3065/3065). On shell it is associated with failure: stderr non-empty 125/325 = 0.385 [0.308,0.473] vs 128/1904 = 0.067, and failure template 83/325 = 0.255 vs 33/1904 = 0.017. But 200/325 output-null shell results have empty stderr, so it is not a failure flag. Failure text is stderr-only: tracebacks 14/14, timeouts 27/27, nonzero returncode 17/17. Probe 3 needs a regex proxy: stderr matching the returncode-N, timeout or census templates fires on 118/6107 = 0.019 [0.013,0.026] (shell 116/2229 = 0.052 [0.038,0.072]). It is unvalidated because there is no reference.
per_corpus.decisive_number: stderr non-empty on looks-successful shell outputs 128/1888 = 0.068; only 33/1888 = 0.017 carry a failure template

per_corpus.answer: exit_code is filled on 87/353 = 0.246 [0.151,0.403] s63, all AG code_exec; 36 nonzero = native true. A, B and C all score P 36/36, R 36/36 (s26), but this is TAUTOLOGICAL: the loader and the marker parse the same 'exitcode:' header. Under null-as-negative, B adds 12 FP (tracebacks in non-code agents' text). Other agents (266 results) have no failure field. Proposed Probe 3 definition: exit_code != 0 on AG code_exec only.
per_corpus.decisive_number: 87/353 results carry an exit code (36 nonzero); agreement 36/36 is by construction

surprises: Gemini (swechat): the native flag and the text exit code never co-occur. 280/816 shell results say 'Exit Code: N!=0' in text but have status=success; the 143 native-true results are edit/cancel failures with no exit text. A and B score precision 0/280 and recall 0/143.

Claude Code is_error is written only on Bash results (false) and on failures (true). Every non-shell result is true or absent: 9128, 1805 and 25768 nulls in swechat_cc, cc_local and aiv_cc. So null means 'not flagged', not 'unknown'.
cc_local: 157 of 311 native-true Bash results are cc_permission_denied (harness refusals). In swechat/claude_code, exit codes dominate (248/300). 'Error' means different things across corpora.

aiv_cc mcp__village__bash results are JSON turn records with the same output/error/system schema as aiv_cu. All 1746 are native-null even when the error field holds a failure, so aiv_cc's native flag has a structural hole exactly where its computer-use traffic is.

Codex has no entry in ir.ERROR_MARKERS (marker recall 0/49), yet its shell text carries the exit code on nearly every result, including zero: 'Exit code: N' on 558/842 and 'Process exited with code N' on 268/842.
OpenCode: the exit code does not reach the IR text. B recall on nonzero-exit shell results is 26/157, and 24 of them have blank text.
The aiv_cu 'system' field is never present in Phase A (0/6107), and the same field in aiv_cc village JSON is null on 0/1746 non-null, i.e. never set. It cannot be tested as a flag.

The census regexes add no recall in any Claude Code corpus, only false positives (swechat/CC shell +81 FP, 0 TP). They help only where native errors start with 'Error:' (aiv_cc MCP: recall 52/256 to 252/256; OpenCode non-shell).
implications_for_phase_b: Use native_error as the Probe 3 error definition wherever it exists, with null counted as 'not error' for Claude Code formats. Text proxies are fallbacks, not replacements.

Split the error class by marker type (exit code / permission denial / tool_use_error / interrupt / native-only). Permission denials are about half of cc_local Bash errors and would otherwise mix harness refusals with command failures.
Gemini needs two separate error classes (native tool-call failure, text exit code). Reporting one pooled 'error rate' would silently change meaning by format.
Codex: native_error plus a nonzero text exit-header fallback for the 163 native-null shell results. Treat Codex numbers as small-n (15 sessions with results in A).

OpenCode: native only. Any Probe 3 mechanism that relies on the model SEEING an error in the result text is weak there, because 24/157 failed shell results show blank text and most show ordinary output.

aiv_cu (and aiv_cc village-bash turns): only an unvalidated stderr regex proxy (118/6107 results) exists. Its stderr rate varies by model family (4/240 to 58/203 on shell). Phase B should report aiv_cu error-dependent results as proxy-based, or drop them.
whowhen: restrict Probe 3 to AG code_exec (87 results, 36 failures in A). The marker/exit agreement there is not evidence.
cursor and simple_text: Probe 3 is dead (no tool results).

If Phase B sets thresholds on error prevalence, use these Phase A native-true rates. Examples: swechat_cc 614/13592 = 0.045 [0.037,0.054]; cc_local 349/5164 = 0.068 [0.056,0.105]; codex 49/1120; opencode 197/3735; gemini 143/2313.
could_not_measure: aiv_cu: precision/recall of any failure definition. There is no reference flag, and no other field behaves like one.
whowhen: real agreement between text and the exit flag. Both come from the same header, so 36/36 is by construction.
swechat/copilot text agreement: 2 sessions, 8 native-true results, below the pre-registered minimum n.
swechat/cursor and simple_text: no tool results in the source.
OpenCode: whether the model saw anything beyond state.output (e.g. exit metadata) for shell results. The IR text carries none, and prompt assembly is not in the data.
Codex: why 163 shell results lack native and exit (unified-exec running/deferred or missing exec_command_end). Not resolved here; see swechat_build.json.
Cluster-bootstrap CIs are degenerate at rates of exactly 0 or 1 (e.g. A precision 488/488 gives [1.00,1.00]); Wilson intervals are in the JSON for those cases.
Precision of the aiv_cc village-bash JSON error-field proxy: native never fires on those turns.

verifier.question: A4 Error-signal survival. Per corpus and per swechat format: fill rates of native_error and exit_code; error_marker distribution; where failure text survives (text start, middle, stderr only); precision and recall of (a) ir.error_marker and (b) marker OR census regexes against the native flag; whether aiv_cu has any failure flag; and the proposed Probe 3 error definition. Re-derived independently from the *_A.parquet caches in scratchpad/a4v (common.py, sw.py, cc.py, cu.py). The measurer's script was read only after my numbers existed.

Null-neg B: P 534/637 = 0.838, cluster [0.736,0.897]; R 534/538 = 0.993, cluster [0.977,0.999]. B-only TPs: computer_use 170, village_bash 38, get_events 10, edit_memory 8, other 12. The loader docstring already says there is no exit field and that 'Exit Code: 1' can carry native False. So P 0/280 is not an empirical finding about text survival. Failure template in stderr on those shell results: 33/1888 = 0.017, cluster [0.010,0.026]. output_null: gui 3065/3065, shell 325. stderr non-empty given output null: 125/325 = 0.385, cluster [0.308,0.473], versus 128/1904 = 0.067 given output present. Proxy fires on 118/6107 = 0.019, cluster [0.013,0.026]; shell 116/2229 = 0.052, cluster [0.038,0.072].
checks.problem: The counts reproduce. The notes' 'failure text lives in stderr only, in every shell family' is overstated: result text also carries no_such_file 3 (29/32 stderr-only), fatal 7, error_line 3, HTTP 2 and perm_denied 1. stderr also carries the harness string 'bash has exited with returncode 0' 4 times. The proxy is unvalidated, as the measurer states.

checks.my_numbers: 353 results, s63. exit_code filled 87/353 = 0.246, cluster [0.151,0.403], all AG code_exec; 36 nonzero. Strict A and B: P 36/36, R 36/36, s26. Null-neg B: 12 FP, all WebSurfer tracebacks in 12 sessions, all 12 flagged extra.log_leak by the loader. Hand-Crafted: 266 results, 0 exit codes in A (no ComputerTerminal results in this split).
checks.problem: The by-construction agreement is correctly flagged. The rule would grade A 'usable'; the measurer downgraded it to 'partial'. That is defensible but off-rule. The 12 FPs are run-script log leakage, not failures of the agents.

overclaims: Verdict labels do not follow the pre-registered usable/partial/absent rule, which grades text proxies: opencode 'usable' (rule: B partial, shell absent), gemini 'partial' (rule: absent, P 0/281, R 0/143), copilot 'partial' (min n not met, so absent), whowhen 'partial' (rule: usable), codex 'usable' (only through exploratory predictor C; question predictor B is partial). They actually grade whether a Probe 3 error definition is available, native or text, and no rule for that was pre-registered.

'The census regexes add no recall in any Claude Code corpus, only false positives' is false for aiv_cc. There B lifts TP from 296 to 534 (R 0.550 to 0.993), and in cc_local B adds 1 TP. The claim holds only for swechat/claude_code.
'Claude Code is_error ... every non-shell result is true or absent' is false for cc_local: 9 non-shell Workflow results have is_error False.

Codex 'text carries the exit code on every shell result, including zero', and the notes' 'every legacy shell result opens with an exit header': actual coverage is 826/842 shell results and 558/561 shell_command results. 13 still-running unified exec outputs and 3 sandbox-timeout texts have no header.

Codex 'R 49/49 (Wilson [0.93,1.00]) s6': Wilson ignores clustering across 6 sessions. 2 of the 49 TPs come only from the recon-derived 'sandbox error: command timed out' string; the exit header alone gives R 47/49.

aiv_cc 'many B false positives are village-bash JSON turns whose error field holds a real failure the harness never flags' is unvalidated. That field is stderr, which the same analysis concludes is not a failure flag. Only 31 B FPs fall on village bash.

aiv_cc CIs (s38, s77) treat runs as independent, but 33473/33475 A results come from one sdk_session_id of one agent. The 'usable' verdict rests on a B precision lower bound of 0.736 against the 0.70 bar, which is less secure than stated.

aiv_cc 'native flag has a structural hole exactly where its computer-use traffic is': mcp__village__computer_use also has 3074 JSON turn records that are never natively flagged, but their error field is non-empty on only 3. So the hole that matters is village bash only.

Gemini 'native flag and text exit code are DISJOINT' is presented as an empirical finding. It follows from the loader's documented mapping: native comes from status, there is no exit field, and 'Exit Code: 1' can carry native False.
aiv_cu notes: 'failure text lives in stderr only, in every shell family' is too strong. no_such_file is 29/32 stderr-only, and fatal, error_line, HTTP and perm_denied also appear in result text.

The question asked for Wilson CIs. The headline reports session-cluster bootstrap, which is appropriate under README rule 5 but gives degenerate [1,1] intervals at P = 1, and switches to Wilson only where the bootstrap collapses (Codex). That gives a mixed and, for small-session units, overconfident account of uncertainty.
